home.heroText: I'm Brais. Developer, maker, geek and professional collector of things I probably shouldn't start. This is where curiosity turns into experiments — and experiments turn into things.
home.featuredText: The first experiment is the place itself: a home for everything I build, learn, break and occasionally finish.
home.hypothesisText: A personal lab is more interesting when it documents attempts, not just achievements.
home.readerText: Can I make reading comics and books feel fundamentally better?
home.learnText: Pick a skill I barely have and make something that forces me to learn it.
home.unknownText: The next experiment is not decided yet. That's part of the fun.
home.manifesto: I like programming. I like comics. I like making things. I like learning. I like telling stories. Instead of turning those interests into ten separate identities, I'm testing what happens when they all feed the same creative practice.
home.followText: Follow an experiment when you care about it. Read the full story, see the failures, grab the files and decide what I should try next. The internet gets enough endless feeds. I want to leave artifacts.

001.title: Make the lab worth visiting.
001.hypothesis: A personal lab is more interesting when it documents attempts, not just achievements.
001.objective: Build a repeatable home for ideas, builds, failures and results — not another polished portfolio.
001.constraint: It has to stay fast, responsive and cheap to host.
001.success: Someone discovers an experiment, gets something useful or entertaining from it, and wants to see what happens next.

002.title: Build a better digital reader.
002.hypothesis: Most digital readers optimise for features. A great reader should optimise for immersion.
002.objective: Prototype a reading engine from scratch and see whether the experience can feel closer to owning the book.
002.constraint: Start small. Web first. No giant platform before the first good reading session.
002.success: A comic or book feels so good to read that the interface gets out of the way.

003.title: Learn by building the thing.
003.hypothesis: Real constraints create better learning than passive study.
003.objective: Pick an unfamiliar skill and ship one small, finished artifact with it.
003.constraint: No waiting until I'm good enough. The artifact is the curriculum.
003.success: A finished thing, a visible before/after and an honest account of what actually accelerated learning.
